title: helm upgrade failure: autorecovery flow, config drift detection gaps, and customer hotpatch rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Several private/VPC customers reported failed platform upgrades when the on-prem Operator applied a Helm chart upgrade. Symptoms varied: partial CRD application, Helm hook timeouts, operator reconciliation loops that never converged, and customers observing configuration divergence after automated post-upgrade reconciliation. In one account the node-level Kubelet rejected a secret update due to an immutable field change which caused the operator to enter a CrashLoopBackOff and block subsequent upgrades.

Impact scope:
- 3 mid-market customers reported outages or degraded control-plane visibility during scheduled upgrades (Feb 18-24).
- Two Dedicated customers impacted in non-prod while testing upgrades.
- Upgrade automation blocked further rollout for our managed Private channel until we validated a fix.

Immediate mitigation done so far:
- Rolled back the operator image to 2.4.0 for the three highest-severity customers (manual Helm rollback documented: link to rollback runbook).
- Opened emergency k8s support tickets with customers with step-by-step diagnostics.
- Disabled automated cluster-wide post-upgrade reconcile job temporarily to stop noisy reconciliations while we investigate root cause.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
1) Helm chart v2.4.1 introduced a CRD ordering change and a new MutatingWebhookConfiguration that requires a short window of webhook readiness. On clusters with slower API servers or heavy load the webhook never reached Ready and Helm hooks timed out.
2) The operator's upgrade controller assumed idempotent secret updates; when the secret schema included an immutable field we attempted a replace instead of create/patch which the API rejected leading to controller restarts.
3) Our config-drift detector ignored certain annotations and therefore failed to surface clusters where manual changes had been made prior to upgrade, producing unexpected diff states and reconciliation thrashing.

Planned fix and rollout steps:
A) Hotfix operator image 2.4.1+rc1 that: (i) adds a guarded retry/backoff around webhook-dependent hooks, (ii) changes secret update to patch/merge strategy when immutable fields are present, (iii) logs clearer reconciliation state transitions for telemetry.
B) Add pre-upgrade cluster readiness check to the upgrade controller that validates webhook pods, CRDEstablished condition, and immutable-secret compatibility before executing Helm upgrade.
C) Expand config-drift detector to include annotation and immutable field diffs; add a preflight warning surfaced in the Console and CLI.
D) Run staged customer rollout: canary on internal infra -> selected non-prod customer clusters -> three affected customer clusters after rollback verification -> all clusters.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for secret patch logic and webhook backoff added.
- Integration test harness updated to simulate slow API server and webhook readiness delays.
- Manual validation checklist for customers to verify rollback and reapply flows.

Observability and follow-ups:
- New telemetry events: upgrade_preflight_status, secret_patch_attempts, reconcile_thrash_count.
- Postmortem to be published in Confluence after rollout and 72h stability window.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hotfix image passes internal canary for 48h with no reconciliation loops.
- Affected customers confirm successful re-apply of v2.4.1+hotfix without data loss.
- Config-drift detector flags previous manual changes in 95% of seeded tests.
